title: Graceful stream evacuation and traffic gating for active-active gateway
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Implement a traffic-gating controller and streaming session evacuation protocol to enable active-active multi-region failover for the hosted API gateway while preserving SLOs. This ticket covers the design and rollout plan for graceful session draining, KV-cache alignment and token-preserving warm handoffs, circuit-breaker integration at the ingress, and a staged load-shedding policy for queued/long-lived streams. Goals: (1) Ensure region failover does not violate 99th-percentile request latency SLOs or increase token-retry costs beyond a 5% delta; (2) Minimize streaming interruptions and avoid orphaned KV caches; (3) Provide deterministic, testable behavior for load-shedding and circuit trips during overloads or partial region outages. Scope: gateway controller changes, session evacuation handshake protocol, rollout canary for 2%/10%/50%/100% traffic, observability and new runbook entries. Out of scope: full client SDK changes beyond fallback headers and minor compatibility shims. Background: Recent incidents showed that naive region drain drops streaming sessions and causes token duplication as clients retry without coherent session handoff. Prior work (ENG-14257 / ENG-100234) introduced KV-sync checkpoints; this ticket operationalizes them into the ingress failover flow and ties gating decisions to SLO-driven metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Canary traffic shift demonstrates <1% increase in observed 99p latency over baseline for both unary and streaming requests
Streaming sessions migrated with end-to-end continuity for at least 95% of sessions in synthetic tests (no dropped messages, token sequence preserved)
Circuit-breaker trips are visible in dashboards and trigger weighted traffic draining without causing client timeouts beyond 2x baseline RTT
Load-shedding policy reduces new session acceptance under sustained overload and keeps CPU/GPU tail latencies within SLO targets
Automated e2e test that simulates region loss is added to CI and passes consistently in staging
risks: Cross-region KV-sync introduces write amplification under heavy load - may increase cost
Client implementations that aggressively reconnect could reissue prefixes and blow through token budgets
Incorrect gating thresholds may cause unnecessary global capacity reduction and increased errors
decisions: Adopt soft-handoff (stitch) model: old region continues servicing existing stream until new region confirms KV checkpoint and accepts a mirrored session for new requests
Circuit-breaker threshold set to 85% of CPU util for streaming workers and 75% for ingress proxies (validated in perf run 2026-02-20)
Load-shedding will be prioritized by session age and client tier; lowest-tier new sessions are rejected first with an HTTP 503+Retry-After
Traffic gating controller will use SLO-driven signal (99th latency + error-rate) combined with capacity windows rather than pure TTL or weight-only shuffles

investigations_and_findings: QA found that mirrored session acceptance in region B failed when checkpoint lag > 300ms because of race on ephemeral key refresh
Perf runs show that continuous KV-sync increases p95 CPU by ~12% but p99 stays within SLO with batching windows of 50ms
Client-side reconnect behavior is the largest external variable; recommended client header 'X-RW-Session-Handoff' to coordinate graceful handoff
open_questions: Should we backpressure upstream load balancers or rely solely on gateway-level gating?
Do we allow partial-accept of streams (mirror only metadata) for ultra-low-latency paths to speed migration?
Is a client SDK change required to achieve 99.9% seamless stream continuity for all customers?
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive pre-warming reduces cold-start interruptions but raises cost; decided to pre-warm only for premium tiers initially
Fallback policy: when mirror handshake fails after N retries, the old region will run a 'buffered termination' window of 10s to let in-flight tokens drain
We avoid forcing single-point global coordinators; controller uses epoched hints and CRDT-style ownership for session IDs
next_steps: Fix race in ephemeral key refresh (ENG-412045) - blocker for 10% canary
Add 'X-RW-Session-Handoff' advisory header to client-facing SDKs and doc the recommended retry behaviour
Run full 50K-stream synthetic migration test in staging and collect p99/p50 latencies and session continuity metrics
Schedule 2% -> 10% -> 50% canary windows with rollback hooks and automated circuit trips linked to throttling playbook
